Precomputing per-block subset lists eliminates repeated bit iteration in add/remove/is_redundant, and using in_set for O(1) membership checks speeds up swap candidate filtering. The faster per-operation cost allows more ILS iterations within the time budget, enabling more exploration and better pruning.

3. The swap search doesn't efficiently filter candidates
4. Only 1-out/1-in swaps are used; 2-in/1-out (add 2, remove 1) could enable better pruning
